content.value_statement: Quantum developers need reliable guidance for circuits, backends, and noisy results. This skill helps plan, optimize, execute, visualize, and debug Qiskit workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains Qiskit setup, package selection, and IBM Quantum account configuration.
Guides creation of circuits with gates, measurements, parameters, and composition.
Shows how to use Sampler and Estimator primitives for simulations and hardware runs.
Covers transpilation, backend selection, job management, and error mitigation guidance.
Supports visualization workflows for circuits, histograms, quantum states, and backend maps.
Outlines VQE, QAOA, Grover search, chemistry, optimization, and machine learning examples.
limitations: Hardware execution requires user credentials and access to IBM Quantum or another provider.
The skill provides guidance and examples; it does not guarantee quantum advantage.
Results from real hardware can be noisy and may require mitigation.
Provider APIs, backend names, and quotas can change after publication.

use_cases.title: Prototype quantum circuits
use_cases.description: Design circuits, choose gates, add measurements, and validate expected outcomes on local simulators.

use_cases.title: Evaluate quantum algorithms
use_cases.description: Plan VQE, QAOA, chemistry, and optimization workflows before moving experiments to hardware.

use_cases.title: Teach Qiskit concepts
use_cases.description: Create clear examples for circuits, primitives, transpilation, visualization, and backend behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Bell circuit
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a two-qubit Bell state in Qiskit, measure both qubits, and explain the expected simulator results.

prompt_templates.title: Select primitives
prompt_templates.prompt: Given my quantum task, help me decide whether to use Sampler or Estimator and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare hardware run
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my circuit for IBM Quantum hardware execution, including backend choice, transpilation settings, shots, and job tracking.

prompt_templates.title: Design VQE workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a VQE experiment in Qiskit for a small molecule, including ansatz choice, optimizer, Estimator use, and convergence checks.

output_examples.input: Explain how to run a Bell circuit on a local simulator.
output_examples.output: A concise plan covering circuit creation, measurement, StatevectorSampler execution, expected counts, and validation of probabilities.

output_examples.input: Review my circuit plan before IBM hardware execution.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering backend compatibility, transpilation, shot count, queue status, error mitigation, and job ID tracking.

output_examples.input: Plan a VQE experiment for a small molecule.
output_examples.output: A workflow that maps the Hamiltonian, chooses an ansatz and optimizer, runs Estimator in a session, and tracks convergence.

best_practices: Start on local simulators, then move to cloud hardware after validating expected measurement behavior.
Transpile for the target backend and review two-qubit gate counts before submitting jobs.
Store job IDs and experiment notes so hardware results can be retrieved and compared later.
anti_patterns: Submitting untested circuits directly to hardware queues.
Using Sampler when the task needs expectation values, or Estimator when it needs bitstrings.
Treating noisy hardware output as final without calibration context or mitigation.

faq.question: Does this skill require an IBM Quantum account?
faq.answer: No for local simulators. Hardware execution needs a provider account and user-managed credentials.

faq.question: Can it help with Qiskit Runtime?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Sampler, Estimator, sessions, batch mode, and basic job management.

faq.question: Does it execute quantum jobs by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and examples; users decide when to run code or submit jobs.

faq.question: What algorithms are covered?
faq.answer: It covers VQE, QAOA, Grover search, quantum chemistry, optimization, and machine learning examples.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I check before real hardware runs?
faq.answer: Check credentials, backend status, transpilation output, shot count, queue time, and error mitigation settings.
